explanation:
[EFFECT] The day of the week influences predicted demand differently for each day — it is a categorical, non-monotonic effect, not a simple weekend-vs-weekday split. Saturday (day 6) consistently produces the largest positive boost to predicted demand, with SHAP contributions clustered around +0.3 to +0.5 across many hours. Weekdays (Monday–Friday) show moderate positive contributions during busy periods but dip negative during quiet hours. Sunday (day 0) has the widest spread of any day, ranging from strongly negative to moderately positive contributions, reflecting highly variable demand depending on the time of day.

[IMPORTANCE] Weekday is the **4th most important feature** out of 9, with a global importance score of 0.173 — placing it just behind hour of the day (by far the top feature), year, and temperature, and meaningfully ahead of month, humidity, weather situation, wind speed, and holiday status. Its influence is substantial but secondary to the time of day.

[RECOMMENDATION] Since Saturday generates the strongest demand signal and Sunday the most unpredictable, operators should ensure maximum bike availability and staffing on Saturdays, while applying flexible, time-of-day-sensitive deployment strategies on Sundays to handle the high variability in demand.
